title: Twitter Social Media: Complete Architecture
description: Design a scalable Twitter-style social media platform with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a scalable Twitter-style microblogging and social platform. The system must allow users to post short messages (tweets) with media, follow other users, view a personalized timeline, like and retweet posts, participate in conversations through replies, exchange direct messages, discover trending topics, and receive real-time notifications. The platform must handle viral events where a single tweet generates millions of impressions and hundreds of thousands of engagements within minutes.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Users can create accounts with profile photos, bios, and verification status
Users can post tweets up to 280 characters with optional images, videos, or polls
Users can follow and unfollow other users; follower/following counts update in real-time
Home timeline displays tweets from followed users in reverse chronological order
Users can like, retweet, quote, and reply to tweets
Hashtags are extracted from tweets and link to topic pages with aggregated posts
Trending topics algorithm surfaces popular hashtags and keywords by region
Users can send and receive direct messages with real-time delivery
Notification system alerts users to likes, retweets, follows, and mentions
Users can search tweets and user profiles by keyword and hashtag

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Home timeline must load in under 100ms at p99 for users with thousands of follows
Tweet delivery must be near real-time with fan-out completion in under 1 second
System must support 600,000+ tweets per minute during major events
Search must return relevant results in under 200ms across billions of tweets
99.9% availability for tweet posting and timeline retrieval
Media uploads must be processed and served via CDN within seconds
Notification delivery must be reliable with at-least-once semantics

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application where tweets, users, follows, notifications, and direct messages share a single deployment and database. This validates the social graph and real-time requirements before introducing the complexity of distributed timeline generation.

terms.term: Frontend
- React 18 with TypeScript
- Vite for build tooling
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- React Query for server state
Backend (ASP.NET Core)
- Minimal API or MVC Controllers
- Entity Framework Core for data access
- Azure SQL Database or AWS RDS for relational data
- Built-in DI, logging, and health checks
Infrastructure
- Azure App Service or AWS EC2/ECS
- Azure Blob Storage or AWS S3 for media uploads
- Azure SignalR Service or AWS AppSync for real-time notifications
- Single database with tables for Users, Tweets, Follows, Likes, Notifications, Messages

data.text: As user growth and tweet volume increase, split the monolith into microservices optimized for read-heavy timelines, write-heavy tweet ingestion, and real-time notifications. The Fan-out-on-write strategy pre-computes timelines for fast reads.

items: Post Service: Handles tweet creation, editing, and deletion. Validates content, extracts hashtags and mentions, and publishes TweetCreated events for downstream services. Stores tweet text and metadata in the primary database.
User Service: Manages user profiles, authentication, follow/unfollow actions, and follower/following counts. Publishes FollowChanged events so the Feed Service can update timelines.

Feed Service: Generates and serves home timelines using a fan-out-on-write strategy. When a user posts, the service pushes the tweet ID into Redis timelines of all followers. Reads are fast Redis sorted-set lookups.

Notification Service: Tracks and delivers real-time notifications for likes, retweets, follows, and mentions. Uses SignalR or WebSocket for push delivery and falls back to email/push for offline users.
Media Service: Handles image and video uploads, transcoding, thumbnail generation, and CDN distribution. Publishes MediaReady events so tweets can reference processed media.
Trending Service: Analyzes tweet volume and velocity for hashtags and keywords. Uses a sliding window to compute trending scores and surfaces top trends by region.
Search Service: Indexes tweets and user profiles for keyword and hashtag search. Uses Elasticsearch for full-text search with filters for date, media type, and language.

Key Patterns
- Optimistic UI for tweet posting with automatic rollback on failure
- Infinite scroll with cursor-based pagination for timeline feeds
- Debounced search input with trending and autocomplete suggestions
- WebSocket / SSE for real-time notifications and new tweet indicators
- Image compression before upload to reduce bandwidth and storage costs
- React Query for caching timelines with background refetch on focus

data.title: Feed Service (ASP.NET Core)

cards.title: Compute
cards.description: Run tweet ingestion, timeline, and notification API servers
pros: Auto-scaling handles viral tweet traffic spikes
cons: Cold starts can delay fan-out during sudden spikes

cards.title: API Gateway
cards.description: Rate limit tweet posting and timeline requests
pros: Edge caching for trending and popular tweet data
WAF protection against bot spam and abuse

cards.title: Cache
cards.description: Cache home timelines, user sessions, and hot tweet data
pros: Sub-millisecond timeline reads for active users
cons: Memory cost for users with large followings

cards.title: Database
cards.description: Store user profiles, tweets, follows, and direct messages
cons: Eventual consistency requires careful conflict resolution

cards.title: Storage
cards.description: Store uploaded images, videos, and media thumbnails
pros: Cheap, durable storage for billions of media files
CDN delivers media with low latency globally

cards.title: Messaging
cards.description: Async fan-out for timelines and notification delivery
pros: Decouples tweet creation from timeline generation
Buffers fan-out bursts during viral events
cons: Fan-out to millions of followers requires careful batching

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Social media timelines are read-heavy; fan-out-on-write trades write cost for read performance
Celebrity users with millions of followers break the fan-out model; use a hybrid push/pull approach
Real-time notifications require WebSocket or SignalR connections with fallback to polling
Media processing is CPU-intensive; offload transcoding to a dedicated service with a queue
Start with a monolith on Azure SQL or AWS DynamoDB, then extract Post, Feed, and Notification as the first microservices
data.takeaway: Twitter Social Media is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
